saints.name: Sts. Processus and Martinian
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Two Roman martyrs venerated from the earliest days and honored on the Aurelian Way…
biography: Processus and Martinian are among the most anciently venerated of the Roman martyrs, buried in a cemetery on the Aurelian Way, where a basilica later rose over their tomb. Roman tradition names them as guards of the Mamertine prison who were converted and baptized, though the historical details of their passion are lost.

Their cult is very old and certain: Pope St. Gregory the Great preached a homily at their tomb, and their relics were eventually translated to St. Peter's Basilica, where they still rest. Their names appear in the ancient sacramentaries and in the Roman Martyrology on this day.
saints.knownFor: Their ancient and continuous veneration in the city of Rome.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
